1:# Brief: routing: broad prompts, universal categories, listing dialog
6:**A. Broad-request prompt routing.** Today the dock needs a hovered game or mod. Make it understand free requests from anywhere (the core, a game, a mod, or nothing selected): "make me a mod for Minecraft where creepers drop diamonds", "work on my frost axe mod and fix the cooldown", "add a shop command to my Rust plugin", "what mods do I have for Valheim", "update the boss mod for the new version". Design `RouteDecision = { intent: create|refine|fix|explain|install|unknown, gameId, categoryId, projectId?, confidence, reason, clarify? }` in `lib/cyrus/route.ts`.
7:- **Cost-aware design (the owner wants lower API spend without a dumber product):** a deterministic fast path first (game aliases from the registry, "my <name> mod" fuzzy-matched against the user's own projects and mod titles, intent verbs, category keywords), costing zero API calls. Only genuinely ambiguous input may use ONE tiny structured classification call through the existing cheapest-model plumbing, or (better when cheap enough) show a one-tap clarification chip ("Frost Axe v2 or Frost Axe?"). The current selection/hover always wins as context.
11:**B. Universal preset categories.** One canonical set, identical across all games (examples the owner gave: Environment, Weapons, Performance; design the final ~14 to 16 so they map cleanly onto the NxLabs mod store; read `lib/cyrus-mods/registry.ts`, the store pages and `lib/cyrus/categories.ts`). For each: id, label, one-line blurb, an **SVG icon** (24x24, `currentColor`, consistent stroke; reuse the existing 12 in `components/icons`/`CategoryIcons.tsx` and draw the missing ones), and per-game availability (a game's `GameSupport.categories` once the game agents land; until then a sensible default table). The **auto-sorter** classifies a finished mod into one primary + up to two secondary categories from the prompt, the generated code and the build metadata, deterministic signals first (zero API), with a cheap fallback only when confidence is low. Mod categories on the map become these presets; migrate existing projects (read-only DB access in dev; write a safe migration helper, do not run it on production).
13:**C. Listing dialog after a mod is built** (and "Edit listing" when clicking an existing mod): title, category (auto-selected, shows "auto-sorted", easy override), icon/logo (upload, or pick a generated/preset glyph, cropped to the rounded shape), brief description (AI draft from the build summary where free, editable, 280 chars). Define `lib/cyrus/listing.ts` NOW and commit it early: `ModListingInput = { title, categoryId, secondaryCategoryIds, iconAssetId|null, description }` plus validators. The **community agent owns storage** (`saveModListing(projectIdOrBuildId, input)` and the NxLabs page); call it through a thin adapter `lib/cyrus/listing-client.ts` that works with a local fallback until their branch is merged. Do not touch the NxLabs page.

Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

## Overview

A Hook is a way for modding frameworks to call your mod's code every time a certain action happens. The `OnEntityTakeDamage` hook is one of the available hooks for Rust plugins.

## Hook Functionality

The `OnEntityTakeDamage` hook occurs when damage is dealt and can block it.

## Hook Parameters

The hook uses the following signature:

```csharp
object OnEntityTakeDamage(BaseCombatEntity entity, HitInfo info)
```

The hook accepts two parameters:
- **BaseCombatEntity**: The entity taking damage
- **HitInfo**: Information about the damage being dealt

## Return Values

A CallHook function will run any code in your plugin that matches the name of the hook and has the same parameters as the hook. The hook can return `null` to allow damage or `false` to block it.

## Documentation Reference

The Oxide Documentation page contains a list of every single hook. You can find the official Oxide documentation at https://umod.org/documentation/games/rust

## Overview

Carbon is a modern modding framework for the game Rust responsible for handling background operations and running custom plugins and extensions with maximum performance.

Carbon uses Harmony and does not require any additional patches to run existing Oxide plugins. ## Official Guidelines

Facepunch maintains a short document called the Community Server and Hosting Guidelines that says in plain terms what you may monetise and what you may not. The source is facepunch.com/legal/servers, last updated 15 July 2025.

You are allowed to monetise your Servers, for example: The guidelines outline specific permitted monetization methods.

## DLC Restrictions

A significant update affects paid DLC: Facepunch updated their Community Server and Hosting Guidelines as of July 15, 2025, with a major change - starting August 7, 2025, you won't be allowed to give players access to paid DLC they don't actually own.

## Community vs. Modded Server Tags

Rust's Community Server List is the in-game directory of vanilla or community-hosted servers that follow Facepunch's guidelines. By default, any Rust server can appear in the Community list if it meets the rules: no gameplay-altering mods, only approved admin tools, and proper configuration.

## Plugin Rules

No gameplay modifying plugins are allowed - any plugin that affects a player's gameplay in any way, such as changes to gather rate, item spawns, player spawns, or smelting mechanics, including selling in-game items, kits, and resources through a custom UI or external storefront. # Hooks in Rust Modding

## What Are Hooks?

A Hook is "a way for modding frameworks to call your mod's code every time a certain action happens."

## Supported Frameworks

Two modding frameworks support hooks:
- **Oxide** - Access documentation at https://umod.org/documentation/games/rust
- **Carbon** - Access documentation at https://docs.carbonmod.gg/

## How Hooks Work

Modding frameworks "insert their special `CallHook` functions throughout the Rust Server code." Code in your plugin will execute if it matches both the hook name and parameters.

## Example Hook Signature

The page provides one detailed example:

```csharp
object OnEntityTakeDamage(BaseCombatEntity hitEntity, HitInfo info)
```

This hook "occurs when damage is dealt but we can block it." The example demonstrates preventing players from damaging boats by checking if the attacked entity is a `MotorRowboat` and returning `false` to block damage.

## Sample Hook Cases

The page mentions these hooks trigger for:
- Entity damage
- Player item pickup
- Locked door opening
- Player boat interaction
- Player waking up
- Player respawning

# Carbon Documentation Overview

## Key Developer Documentation Sections

The Carbon framework provides comprehensive developer resources accessible at `/devs/local-server-hosting`:

**Core Development Topics:**
- **Plugin Development**: Carbon supports the `carbon/plugins` folder structure, maintaining Oxide compatibility
- **Hot Reload**: Allows "Harmony mods to be reloaded on the fly when changes are made"
- **Hooks Reference**: Dynamic hook system at `/references/hooks` loads only hooks used by plugins
- **Oxide Compatibility**: "Easy to make the switch from Oxide to Carbon by keeping the folder/plugin structure the same"

## Main Documentation Links

| Section | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Owner Docs | `/owners/getting-started` |
| Developer Docs | `/devs/local-server-hosting` |
| Hooks Reference | `/references/hooks` |
| Commands | `/references/commands/` |
| ConVars | `/references/convars/` |
| Rust References | `/references/` (Items, Entities, Prefabs, etc.) |

## Community & Resources

- **Discord**: discord.gg/carbonmod
- **GitHub**: github.com/CarbonCommunity/Carbon.Documentation
- **Release Downloads**: Available at `/owners/getting-started#releases`

**Note**: The page content doesn't specify the current version number or detailed CarbonPlugin vs RustPlugin distinctions—check the full developer documentation for those specifics.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Rust's forced wipe schedule:

Facepunch ships its monthly update on the first Thursday of every month at 19:00 UK time, and that patch forces a wipe on every Rust server. The update that contains the force wipe starts at 11 AM PT / 2 PM ET and is usually over within an hour or so.

There are no exceptions and no opt-out. The UK observes British Summer Time, so in UTC that lands at 18:00 from late March to late October and 19:00 UTC the rest of the year.

The upcoming force wipes for the remainder of 2026 include:
- October 1, 2026 and November 5, 2026, December 3, 2026

So you are correct about the schedule: **first Thursday of every month at 2 PM ET** is when Facepunch forces the wipe with their monthly update.

# Weather Convars in Rust

Based on the wiki documentation, here are all weather convars with their value ranges:

## Basic Weather Loading
- `weather.load` - loads specific weather type (Clear, Dust, Fog, Overcast, RainHeavy, RainMild, Storm)
- `weather.reset` - reverts to dynamic weather
- `weather.report` - displays current dynamic weather

## Gameplay Impact
- `weather.wetness_rain` - adjusts how wet players become from rain
- `weather.wetness_snow` - adjusts how wet players become from snow

## Probability Parameters
- `weather.clear_chance`
- `weather.dust_chance`
- `weather.fog_chance`
- `weather.overcast_chance`
- `weather.storm_chance`
- `weather.rain_chance`

## Detailed Environmental Controls
According to the documentation, "negative values (-1) indicate that the value isn't overwritten and is using whatever the dynamic weather system is currently outputting."

- `weather.rain` - precipitation intensity
- `weather.wind` - wind strength (primarily visual)
- `weather.thunder` - lightning/thunder frequency
- `weather.rainbow` - forces rainbow appearance
- `weather.fog` - fog density
- `weather.atmosphere_rayleigh` - sky color scattering intensity
- `weather.atmosphere_mie` - sky color scattering intensity
- `weather.atmosphere_brightness` - sky brightness
- `weather.atmosphere_contrast` - sky contrast
- `weather.atmosphere_directionality` - sun glow size
- `weather.cloud_size` - cloud layer scale
- `weather.cloud_opacity` - cloud transparency
- `weather.cloud_coverage` - sky coverage percentage
- `weather.cloud_sharpness` - cloud definition
- `weather.cloud_coloring` - light blending
- `weather.cloud_attenuation` - cloud darkness
- `weather.cloud_scattering` - sunlight scatter/bloom
- `weather.cloud_brightness` - overall cloud brightness

# <FilePenLineIcon class="carbon-icon" /> Creating Your First Plugin

If you’re looking at creating Oxide-compatible plugins, it’s as easy as you’ve always known it.
It uses the same syntax, naming and formatting as regular Oxide plugins.

::: code-group

```csharp:line-numbers [MyPlugin.cs]
namespace Oxide.Plugins;

[Info("MyPlugin", "<author>", "1.0.0")]
[Description("<optional_description>")]
public class MyPlugin : RustPlugin
{
    private void OnServerInitialized()
    {
        Puts("Hello world!");
    }
}
```

:::

## <StarIcon class="carbon-icon" /> CarbonPlugin

If you’re looking to create Carbon-only plugins, which **extend** the functionality of regular Oxide plugins and provide
additional tools to ease development, you can use `CarbonPlugin` as your base class.

::: code-group

```csharp:line-numbers [MyPlugin.cs]
namespace Carbon.Plugins;

[Info("MyPlugin", "<author>", "1.0.0")]
[Description("<optional_description>")]
public class MyPlugin : CarbonPlugin
{
    private void OnServerInitialized()
    {
        Puts("Hello world!");
    }
}
```

# Oxide Porting
![Oxide Porting](/misc/oxide-to-carbon.webp){width=1640px height=502px}

This is an in-depth walkthrough of migrating an Oxide server over to Carbon.

After following **Prerequisites** and **Carbon Files Installation** sections below, follow either the **Automatic Migration** or **Manual Migration** section as desired.

:::danger Prerequisites
Both migration options require first reverting Oxide-patched Facepunch DLLs to vanilla versions. **Oxide and Carbon can NOT coexist** in the same server install, because they do the same thing (albeit via different approaches). Please carefully read the **Migration Prerequisites** section below.
:::

## Migration Prerequisites

The following operations are required prior to **Carbon Files Installation** and either **Automatic** or **Manual Migration**.

### Shutdown

You must shut down your server before migrating.

### Disable Oxide Tooling

You **must** ensure that any tooling that automatically installs/updates Oxide is disabled. **Carbon and Oxide can NOT coexist.** Allowing the server to run with both of them installed will break your server!

Detailed instructions cannot be provided here; there are many different implementations of this, and they are out of scope for this documentation.

:::tip Carbon has Self Updating as a built-in feature. See **Feature Comparison** below.
:::

### Revert Oxide-patched Facepunch DLLs

Oxide ships pre-patched versions of Facepunch DLLs, but Carbon patches them dynamically. **Your Facepunch DLLs must therefore be reverted to vanilla versions.** The easiest way to revert is to run a `steamcmd` update operation on your server with the `validate` option included.

An example is provided below. **This is just an example.** Your server may differ in install location, beta/branch, etc.
```
steamcmd +force_install_dir C:\games\rust +login anonymous +app_update 258550 -beta public validate +quit
```

:::tip If steamcmd fails to validate, delete the `steamapps` directory from the root of the server install and try again.

For a deeper clean, you can completely remove the `Managed` folder under `RustDedicated_Data` before running the validate - but note that **this will also wipe out any extension DLLs**, so be sure to copy those somewhere else first. See the **Extensions** section below.
:::

:::info Carbon and Facepunch DLLs
With Carbon, your `RustDedicated_Data/Managed` folder will always be untouched from Facepunch's shipped configuration.
:::

## Key Points:

**Easy Anti-Cheat Compatibility with Oxide:**
EAC is compatible with uMod (Oxide) plugins, and you don't need to disable EAC to use server-side plugins.

**Server-Side Only Installation:**
Oxide (maintained today as uMod) is a modding framework that loads C# plugins into the Rust server without touching the game client. Players still join with the normal Rust game; the changes live entirely on the server. This means Oxide lives on the server, not the client.

**Client-Side Modifications:**
Some client-side mods may require EAC to be disabled. Always verify whether a mod needs EAC disabled before installing it.

**Plugin Installation:**
Plugin .cs files hot-load into oxide/plugins without a restart.

In summary, Oxide/uMod plugins are server-side only modifications that don't require players to install anything on their clients, and they're fully compatible with Easy Anti-Cheat remaining enabled on the server.

# Key Points from the Rust Wipe Guide

**Server Must Update to Stay Joinable:**
"Once the patch lands, players on the new client cannot join a server still running last month's build."

**Protocol Mismatch Issue:**
The update "increments Rust's protocol number, so clients on the old version can no longer connect."

**Oxide/Framework Updates:**
After a forced wipe, "Oxide or Carbon may need a moment to pull the new compatible build; one more restart usually clears framework errors."

**Plugin Breaking After Update:**
Administrators should "Open the Console and check for plugin compile errors" immediately after the server returns from a monthly forced wipe.

**Timing in UTC:**
Force wipes occur at "19:00 UTC" during winter months, with a shift to "18:00 UTC during British Summer Time (late March to late October)."

**Blueprint Wipes:**
"The blueprint wipe is a convention most servers follow. A blueprint wipe is only strictly required when Facepunch changes the item or blueprint system."

# Cyrus × Rust: readiness and how Rust modding works

Agent: game-rust (Cyrus v6). Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-rust`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-game-rust`.
Research date: 2026-10-08. Current Rust build: **2634.289.1** (October 2026 forced update, 1 Oct). Next forced update: **Thu 5 Nov 2026, 19:00 UTC**.

Rust stays **`soon`** in `lib/cyrus/games.ts`. Making it `live` is the owner's call. The list below is what's still missing.

---

## Part 1: How Rust modding works (one page, also usable on the marketing page)

**A Rust mod is a server plugin.** It's one C# source file (`MyPlugin.cs`). The server compiles it, so you don't build it first. Two frameworks run these plugins:

- **Oxide (uMod).** The long-standing standard, MIT open source. It ships patched copies of the game's server DLLs. Plugins live in `oxide/plugins`, settings in `oxide/config`, saved data in `oxide/data`, translations in `oxide/lang`, logs in `oxide/logs`.
- **Carbon.** A newer framework that runs the same Oxide plugins unchanged. Instead of shipping patched DLLs it patches the game at runtime, and it uses `carbon/plugins` and similar folders. Oxide and Carbon can't be installed on the same server. Nxeon offers Oxide today. Carbon isn't offered yet.

**Install and reload.** Drop the `.cs` file into the plugins folder. Within seconds the framework compiles it (Roslyn, C# 14) and loads it. Edit the file and it hot-reloads. No restart, no downtime. On first load the plugin writes its own config file, and you edit that to tune it.

**Players install nothing.** Rust has no client modding: the game client is protected by Easy Anti-Cheat and has no mod loader. Plugins still change a lot of what players experience:
- menus, HUDs and overlays (CUI, drawn by the server and sent to each player),
- chat commands and messages,
- custom versions of existing items (renamed, re-skinned with Steam Workshop skins, given new behaviour),
- spawned NPCs, vehicles, crates and events,
- gather rates, loot, crafting, raid rules and weather.

They can't add new 3D models, textures or sounds that aren't already in the game.

**How a plugin plugs in.** The framework calls named methods ("hooks") when things happen in the game: `OnEntityTakeDamage` when something is hit, `OnPlayerInput` on key presses, `OnLootSpawn` when a crate fills, and so on. There are about 737 hooks today. A hook that returns a value can cancel the game's action, for example blocking damage.

**Permissions** follow `<plugin>.<permission>` (for example `frostaxe.use`) and are granted with `oxide.grant group default frostaxe.use`.

**The monthly cycle (the main reason plugins break).** Facepunch ships a forced update on the **first Thursday of every month**: 18:00 UTC in UK summer time, 19:00 UTC otherwise. On that day:
1. Every server must update. Clients on the new build can't join old servers because the protocol number changes (2633 → 2634 in October).
2. Oxide must update the same day, because it ships patched game DLLs. 2.0.7783 came out within hours on 1 Oct, followed by hotfix builds.
3. Plugins that used game code Facepunch changed stop compiling and unload.

Real examples from Oxide's own patch manifest:
- **September (2633):** `ItemContainer.CanAcceptItem` and `PlayerInventory.CanWearItem/CanEquipItem` gained a player parameter, and the `OnComposterUpdate` hook was removed.
- **October (2634):** `ItemContainer.Insert/Remove` gained a player parameter, and new Gen2 livestock animals arrived with their own hooks.

**Server rules (Facepunch's Community Server Guidelines, updated 15 Jul 2025).**
- Servers that change gameplay must be listed as **Modded**. Oxide does this by default (`"Modded": true`) and warns at startup when it's off.
- You may charge fees, take donations and sell cosmetics.
- You may **not** give players paid Facepunch DLC they don't own, pretend to be an official server, or circumvent paid content.

**Safety.** Oxide plugins aren't sandboxed. A plugin can read files, open network connections or start programs with the server's rights. That's why every Cyrus plugin goes through a strict static check before anyone sees it.

---

## Part 2: What Cyrus does for Rust now (this branch)

| Piece | File |
|---|---|
| Verified GameSupport (default export), plus version table, forced-update calendar, paths and the `knowledge` pack (40 API sheet lines, 10 failure rules) | `lib/cyrus/games/rust.ts` |
| 737 hook names Oxide/Carbon really call (generated) | `lib/cyrus/games/rust.hooks.ts` |
| Static validator (structure, manifest, dangerous APIs, failure rules, hooks, permissions, data folder, cleanup) | `lib/cyrus/games/rust.validate.ts` |
| Generator upgraded: verified APIs only, `oxide/…` layout, `cyrus.mod.json` manifest, target build in the header, unload cleanup, safe class names | `lib/cyrus/engine/games/rust.ts` |
| Compile harness (Roslyn against a reviewed stub surface; real-DLL mode ready) | `tools/cyrus/rust-check/` |
| Unit tests (pure) | `test/cyrus-game-rust.test.ts` |
| Monthly refresh script | `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/game-rust/refresh-rust-facts.sh` |

**What the generator fixed (the handoff code had none of these flagged as `plausible:`, so every API was checked):**
- `PhoneController.PositionToGridName` → `MapHelper.PositionToString` (unconfirmed → used by 14 plugins).
- `BUTTON.FIRE_THIRD` (middle mouse) → `BUTTON.RELOAD` (R). FIRE_THIRD appears in no current plugin or call site.
- Wolf prefab `wolf/wolf.prefab` → `wolf/wolf2.prefab`. The old one no longer exists.
- Removed the horse prefab `nextai/testridablehorse` (gone).
- Frost: `temperature.SetValue` + `SendChangesToClient` (unconfirmed; temperature is recomputed every tick anyway) → cold damage + `wetness.Add`.
- Fire: `FireBall.lifeTimeMin/Max` (unconfirmed) → spawn, track, kill on a timer and in `Unload()`.
- Flight: `ApplyInheritedVelocity` (unconfirmed; player movement is client-side) → vehicle lift only.
- `damageTypes.Add` (unconfirmed) → `damageTypes.Set` when the hit doesn't carry that type yet, otherwise `Hurt` on the next tick, so hooks never nest.
- `task.owner` → `crafter.owner` (the hook's third argument, confirmed in the decompiled call site and in ZLevels).
- `Plugin.Call<bool>` throws when the other plugin returns null (Oxide `Plugin.cs` uses `Convert.ChangeType`) → raw `Call` + type test.
- Boombox station switching with `http://radio.example.com` URLs removed. It pointed the server at an external stream and used an unconfirmed API.
- Custom items had a random fake Workshop skin ID (2,000,000,000+). Now the skin ID defaults to 0 and the item is identified by shortname + display name (+ skin, if the owner sets a real Workshop skin). No fake Workshop IDs get sent to clients, and no DLC skins are used.
- A mod named "Item" (or any game type name) would have produced `class Item : RustPlugin`, shadowing the game's `Item` class. Names like that now become `ItemPlugin`.

Every prefab path and item shortname the generator can emit was checked against Carbon's index for 2634.289.1. All 30 prefabs and 36 shortnames are present.

---

## Part 3: Verification harness assessment

| Level | Needs | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Static lint (`rust.validate.ts`) | nothing | **Done**, runs in tests and can run on every build/edit |
| Roslyn compile against Cyrus's stub surface (`tools/cyrus/rust-check`, mode 1) | .NET 8 SDK (free, MIT) | **Built.** SDK installed user-locally on node-2 at `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/cyrus-v6-game-rust/node_modules/.cyrus-dotnet` (no system change). Catches syntax, typos, wrong types/overloads against the reviewed API list. |
| Roslyn compile against the real game (mode 2) | Rust Dedicated Server `RustDedicated_Data/Managed/*.dll` + Oxide release DLLs | **Not run.** Needs the owner's OK (below). |
| Load test on a real server (plugin loads, self-test passes) | A throwaway Rust server + Oxide | **Not run.** |

**What the owner would need to provide for mode 2 (a real compile).** Nothing has to be bought. The Rust Dedicated Server is free (Steam app **258550**, anonymous login, as used by Oxide's own build). On the build host:
```
steamcmd +force_install_dir /tank/nxeon-build/rust-ref +login anonymous +app_update 258550 -beta public validate +quit
# + unzip the matching Oxide.Rust-linux.zip from github.com/OxideMod/Oxide.Rust/releases over it
tools/cyrus/rust-check/run.sh --refs /tank/nxeon-build/rust-ref/RustDedicated_Data/Managed
```
Notes:
- The download is several GB, and it's refreshed once a month after the forced update.
- These are Facepunch's proprietary files. They stay on the build host, are **never committed, never copied into a customer download, never redistributed**. The tool only references them at compile time.
- Decision needed: OK to keep a reference copy of RustDedicated on node-2's `tank` dataset?

**Mode 3 (load test)** would start that server headless with a tiny procedural map (`+server.level "Procedural Map" +server.worldsize 1000 +server.maxplayers 1`), copy the plugin plus its `tests/<Name>SelfTest.cs`, and run `<cmd>.selftest` over RCON.
- It needs about 4-6 GB RAM for a few minutes, so it doesn't fit inside the 7 GB agents slice next to other work. It would need its own slot or a small dedicated VM.
- Owner decision.

---

## Part 4: Checklist before Rust can go live

**Owner decisions**
- [ ] Approve a reference RustDedicated copy on the build host for real compiles (mode 2), or say no and accept stub-compile + lint only.
- [ ] Approve (or not) a load-test sandbox: its own small VM or a time-boxed slot. Never on a customer VM.
- [ ] Decide on Carbon support. Nxeon only offers Oxide today, and the GameSupport says so (Carbon folders are documented but untested).
- [ ] Flip `rust` to `live` in `lib/cyrus/games.ts`, after the items below.

**Engineering**
- [ ] Wire `validateRustProject` into the real build path, so a `block` finding stops delivery and a `warn` finding is shown on the build card. This is the efficiency/lifecycle agents' pipeline; the call is one line: `validateRustProject(files)`.
- [ ] Wire `knowledge.apiSheet` into the generation prompt and `failureRules[].fix` into the repair prompt. Owner: efficiency agent.
- [ ] Hook the real-AI path (not just the templates) through the same validator and the stub compile.
- [ ] Install flow: copy `manifest.install` (+ optional `optionalInstall`) to `/opt/rust/<path>` on the customer's server. No restart is needed. Then read `oxide/logs` / the console for `Loaded plugin <Title> v<x> by Cyrus` (already parsed by `lib/mod-health.ts`). Owner: lifecycle agent.
- [ ] Outdated warnings: on each forced update (use `nextRustForcedUpdate()`), mark every installed Cyrus Rust plugin whose `targetGameVersion` ≠ `RUST_CURRENT_VERSION` as "needs re-check", and notify creators. Owner: lifecycle agent.
- [ ] Gameplay plugins carry `serverListing: "modded"`. The install flow should warn if the server's `oxide.config.json` has `"Modded": false`.
- [ ] One end-to-end test on a real Nxeon Rust server you own (not a customer's): install a generated plugin, run its self-test, unload, confirm cleanup (no stray NPCs/UI).

**Maintenance (monthly, about 30 min after Oxide releases on wipe day)**
- [ ] Run `refresh-rust-facts.sh <worktree>`. Review the hook diff and any "PREFAB GONE" / "ITEM GONE" lines.
- [ ] Add the new build to `RUST_VERSIONS` (mark it `current`, the old one `unsupported`) and update `RUST_VERSION_LABEL` / `RUST_MIN_LOADER`.
- [ ] Turn real signature changes into `knowledge.failureRules`. Regenerate `rust.hooks.ts`.
- [ ] Re-run `test/cyrus-game-rust.test.ts` and `tools/cyrus/rust-check/run.sh` (plus mode 2 if approved).

---

## Sources
- Oxide: https://github.com/OxideMod/Oxide.Rust (+ `resources/Rust.opj` history), Oxide.Core, Oxide.CSharp; releases https://github.com/OxideMod/Oxide.Rust/releases
- Carbon: https://docs.carbonmod.gg (first plugin, Oxide porting), metadata https://api.carbonmod.gg/meta/carbon/hooks.json, `/meta/rust/{prefabs,entities,items}.json`; releases https://github.com/CarbonCommunity/Carbon/releases
- Facepunch: https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust/Hooks, https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust/Weather, https://facepunch.com/legal/servers
- Wipe calendar: https://www.gameserverkings.com/knowledge-base/rust/wipe-day-guide/
- API usage corpus: 69 current plugins from https://umod.org/plugins (Kits, NTeleportation, RaidableBases, ZLevelsRemastered, Clans, Friends, …)

## Unknowns (also in GameSupport.unknowns)
- Rust's game assemblies are closed. Member names are cross-checked against decompiled call sites and current plugins, not compiled against the real DLLs.
- Facepunch's plugin-guidelines support article returned 403. The Community-vs-Modded rule comes from Oxide's own startup warning and secondary sources.
- Carbon on Nxeon is untested.
- Whether players can rename items in 2634, which would let them fake a name-identified custom item. Setting a Workshop skin ID closes this.

- Wolf prefab `wolf/wolf.prefab` → `wolf/wolf2.prefab`. The old one no longer exists.
- Removed the horse prefab `nextai/testridablehorse` (gone).
- Frost: `temperature.SetValue` + `SendChangesToClient` (unconfirmed; temperature is recomputed every tick anyway) → cold damage + `wetness.Add`.
- Fire: `FireBall.lifeTimeMin/Max` (unconfirmed) → spawn, track, kill on a timer and in `Unload()`.
- Flight: `ApplyInheritedVelocity` (unconfirmed; player movement is client-side) → vehicle lift only.
- `damageTypes.Add` (unconfirmed) → `damageTypes.Set` when the hit doesn't carry that type yet, otherwise `Hurt` on the next tick, so hooks never nest.
- `task.owner` → `crafter.owner` (the hook's third argument, confirmed in the decompiled call site and in ZLevels).
- `Plugin.Call<bool>` throws when the other plugin returns null (Oxide `Plugin.cs` uses `Convert.ChangeType`) → raw `Call` + type test.
- Boombox station switching with `http://radio.example.com` URLs removed. It pointed the server at an external stream and used an unconfirmed API.
- Custom items had a random fake Workshop skin ID (2,000,000,000+). Now the skin ID defaults to 0 and the item is identified by shortname + display name (+ skin, if the owner sets a real Workshop skin). No fake Workshop IDs get sent to clients, and no DLC skins are used.
- A mod named "Item" (or any game type name) would have produced `class Item : RustPlugin`, shadowing the game's `Item` class. Names like that now become `ItemPlugin`.

Every prefab path and item shortname the generator can emit was checked against Carbon's index for 2634.289.1. All 30 prefabs and 36 shortnames are present.

## Part 3: Verification harness assessment

| Level | Needs | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Static lint (`rust.validate.ts`) | nothing | **Done**, runs in tests and can run on every build/edit |
| Roslyn compile against Cyrus's stub surface (`tools/cyrus/rust-check`, mode 1) | .NET 8 SDK (free, MIT) | **Built.** SDK installed user-locally on node-2 at `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/cyrus-v6-game-rust/node_modules/.cyrus-dotnet` (no system change). Catches syntax, typos, wrong types/overloads against the reviewed API list. |
| Roslyn compile against the real game (mode 2) | Rust Dedicated Server `RustDedicated_Data/Managed/*.dll` + Oxide release DLLs | **Not run.** Needs the owner's OK (below). |
| Load test on a real server (plugin loads, self-test passes) | A throwaway Rust server + Oxide | **Not run.** |

**What the owner would need to provide for mode 2 (a real compile).** Nothing has to be bought. The Rust Dedicated Server is free (Steam app **258550**, anonymous login, as used by Oxide's own build). On the build host:
```
steamcmd +force_install_dir /tank/nxeon-build/rust-ref +login anonymous +app_update 258550 -beta public validate +quit
# + unzip the matching Oxide.Rust-linux.zip from github.com/OxideMod/Oxide.Rust/releases over it
tools/cyrus/rust-check/run.sh --refs /tank/nxeon-build/rust-ref/RustDedicated_Data/Managed
```
Notes:
- The download is several GB, and it's refreshed once a month after the forced update.
- These are Facepunch's proprietary files. They stay on the build host, are **never committed, never copied into a customer download, never redistributed**. The tool only references them at compile time.
- Decision needed: OK to keep a reference copy of RustDedicated on node-2's `tank` dataset?

**Mode 3 (load test)** would start that server headless with a tiny procedural map (`+server.level "Procedural Map" +server.worldsize 1000 +server.maxplayers 1`), copy the plugin plus its `tests/<Name>SelfTest.cs`, and run `<cmd>.selftest` over RCON.
- It needs about 4-6 GB RAM for a few minutes, so it doesn't fit inside the 7 GB agents slice next to other work. It would need its own slot or a small dedicated VM.
- Owner decision.

---

## Part 4: Checklist before Rust can go live

**Owner decisions**
- [ ] Approve a reference RustDedicated copy on the build host for real compiles (mode 2), or say no and accept stub-compile + lint only.
- [ ] Approve (or not) a load-test sandbox: its own small VM or a time-boxed slot. Never on a customer VM.
- [ ] Decide on Carbon support. Nxeon only offers Oxide today, and the GameSupport says so (Carbon folders are documented but untested).
- [ ] Flip `rust` to `live` in `lib/cyrus/games.ts`, after the items below.

**Engineering**
- [ ] Wire `validateRustProject` into the real build path, so a `block` finding stops delivery and a `warn` finding is shown on the build card. This is the efficiency/lifecycle agents' pipeline; the call is one line: `validateRustProject(files)`.
- [ ] Wire `knowledge.apiSheet` into the generation prompt and `failureRules[].fix` into the repair prompt. Owner: efficiency agent.
- [ ] Hook the real-AI path (not just the templates) through the same validator and the stub compile.
- [ ] Install flow: copy `manifest.install` (+ optional `optionalInstall`) to `/opt/rust/<path>` on the customer's server. No restart is needed. Then read `oxide/logs` / the console for `Loaded plugin <Title> v<x> by Cyrus` (already parsed by `lib/mod-health.ts`). Owner: lifecycle agent.
- [ ] Outdated warnings: on each forced update (use `nextRustForcedUpdate()`), mark every installed Cyrus Rust plugin whose `targetGameVersion` ≠ `RUST_CURRENT_VERSION` as "needs re-check", and notify creators. Owner: lifecycle agent.
- [ ] Gameplay plugins carry `serverListing: "modded"`. The install flow should warn if the server's `oxide.config.json` has `"Modded": false`.
- [ ] One end-to-end test on a real Nxeon Rust server you own (not a customer's): install a generated plugin, run its self-test, unload, confirm cleanup (no stray NPCs/UI).

- [ ] Run `refresh-rust-facts.sh <worktree>`. Review the hook diff and any "PREFAB GONE" / "ITEM GONE" lines.
- [ ] Add the new build to `RUST_VERSIONS` (mark it `current`, the old one `unsupported`) and update `RUST_VERSION_LABEL` / `RUST_MIN_LOADER`.
- [ ] Turn real signature changes into `knowledge.failureRules`. Regenerate `rust.hooks.ts`.

### Cyrus v5: the owner's redesign (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v5`)

The owner's own Cyrus redesign (handoff `/tank/handoffs/cyrus/cyrus-handoff/`, START-HERE.md) replaces the v4 studio at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** (+ `/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`, and the core gallery at **`/dashboard/cyrus/cores`**). Same preview gate (`requireModBuilderUser()` on every page, `modBuilderUser()` on every API). The portal sidebar and top bar stay; the studio fills the app frame.

**Where it lives.** UI `components/cyrus/{chrome,cosmos,cores,icons,preview,prompt}` + `CyrusApp.tsx` (handoff components, imports re-rooted); state/engine `lib/cyrus/{store,forge,fx,data,types,camera,hooks,zip,highlight}.ts` + `lib/cyrus/engine/` (template generators); game logos `public/cyrus/games/`. Kept from v4: `components/cyrus/kit/` (icon set used by the token modal, the install-to-server modal), `lib/cyrus/{projects,meta,models,estimate,uploads,diff,tokens/}`.

**Scoping (nothing leaks into the portal).** `app/dashboard/cyrus/layout.tsx` wraps every Cyrus route in `.cyrus-root.nx-dark-island` and loads Inter / Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono as CSS variables on that box only. `studio.css` (handoff globals + network CSS) and `cores/cores.css` are generated from the handoff with every selector under `.cyrus-root`, keyframes and `@property` renamed `cy5-*`, and the three class names that collide with portal globals renamed (`cy5-glass`, `cy5-btn-ghost`, `cy5-kbd`). The root uses `container-type: size; contain: layout paint`, so the handoff's `position: fixed` chrome is contained in the content area; `100vw/vh` became `cqw/cqh`. Tailwind colour tokens are `cy-*` (`text-cy-ink`, `border-cy-line` …, `@theme inline` in `app/globals.css` pointing at variables that exist only on `.cyrus-root`), plus a `cy-light:` variant. `nx-dark-island` keeps the portal's generated light-mode retargeting off the studio (it has its own light theme). `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a studio selector is unscoped or a keyframe isn't `cy5-`.

**Theme.** The portal's: `html[data-theme="light"]` / localStorage `nx-theme`. The studio's toggle presses the portal's own toggle button; `useCyrusBoot` mirrors `data-theme` into the store for the canvas and shaders. No `cyrus-theme` key.

**Real vs template.** Minecraft is the one real game (`GAMES[].real`). The account's builds are its Minecraft mods (`lib/cyrus/real.ts deriveReal`: one mod per project, builds = versions, category from the build's own words, at most two extra category branches). Minecraft seeds are dashed **ideas**: clicking one writes a buildable prompt. Notes / restore / favourite are the existing `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root`; files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`; downloads are the real `.jar` / source zip; **Deploy** opens the v4 install modal. Every other game (and added games) is the handoff's template generator, labelled "Template preview", spends no tokens, kept in localStorage per account (`cyrus-state-v1:<userId>`).

**Forge stream** (`POST /api/cyrus/generate`, NDJSON, handoff §6 GenEvents). A prompt that routes to Minecraft, or a change to a real mod, goes through `lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild` (extracted from `POST /api/mod-builder/builds`, which now calls it too: same validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap and token gate); token errors answer JSON 402/403/429 before the stream so `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError` opens the modal. Then `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` streams the real build: stage changes → `think`, the service `/live` draft → `file`/`chunk`, in-place edits → `file-set`, keep-alive `ping`, final source + `done {tokens: charged}` or `error`. `GET ?follow=<id>` re-attaches (page load with a running build, dropped connection; the client retries 4×). Template games run the handoff's `forgeStream()` (no model call). Additive event types: `build`, `file-set`, `ping`.

**Tokens** (UI-CONTRACT.md): `<CyrusTokensHost/>` in `CyrusApp`; `<CyrusTokenChip compact/>` replaces the handoff's credit counter in the top bar; `<CyrusTokenEstimate/>` in the prompt dock for real targets; `<CyrusModelLock/>` + typical token range per model + `<CyrusModelPanelFoot/>` in the model picker; `cyrusTokens.refresh()` after each real build. The local `credits` counter is gone. Model ids/names stay the economy's: Katara / Saka / Yakko.

**Verification** (node-2, devhost): throwaway DB seeded by `.cyrus-verify/seed.ts` (not committed), a local stand-in of the build service (`.cyrus-verify/mock-svc.mjs`, same HTTP as the VM; the portal's real create/sync/live/source/jar code runs unchanged), Playwright screenshots in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-redesign/shots/`.

- `BUTTON.RELOAD` (R) as the ability key works per the corpus; how it feels in-game is untested.
- Nothing has been run on a real Rust server.
